study_identification_part.si4_title: Gray matter atrophy is constrained by normal structural brain network architecture in depression

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To investigate the association between gray matter atrophy and normal connectome architecture at the individual level in depression, identify putative disease epicenters whose structural connectome profiles resemble atrophy patterns, and examine whether brain regions with stronger connections to these epicenters show greater vulnerability to disease.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis:
Answer: Statistical methods included: (1) Backward stepwise regression to identify disease epicenters whose connectivity maps predict regional atrophy (R² and significance recorded); (2) Paired t-tests to compare model performance (structural vs functional, single vs multi-epicenter); (3) Permutation testing (1000 iterations) with Bonferroni correction to identify significantly shared epicenters; (4) Pearson correlation between disease exposure (connectivity-weighted atrophy of epicenters) and regional Z-scores for each patient; (5) Comparison of epicenter degree and participation coefficient vs randomly selected regions (1000 permutations); (6) K-means clustering (repeated 100 times, K=2-10, silhouette-based selection) on per-patient connectivity-atrophy correlation patterns to identify subgroups; (7) Two-sample t-tests with FDR correction to compare demographic/clinical variables between subgroups.
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: Comprehensive statistical methods are described throughout the Methods section with specific tests, correction methods, and parameters.
Supporting Text: For the multiple-epicenter model, we performed a backfoward stepwise regression analysis... The performance of these models was compared using paired t test... we investigated whether they were significantly shared by patients with depression above chance using permutation testing (1000 times)... p value (corrected for Bonferroni)... we calculated the Pearson's correlation coefficient between the disease exposure and atrophy severity (Z-scores)... The k-means clustering analysis was performed... where the optimal number of clusters was determined (between 2 and 10) according to silhouette values. The k-means clustering was repeated 100 times... We investigated whether demographic characteristics... differed among uncovered subgroups.
Location: Methods sections: lines 129-170
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief:
Answer: Structural covariance architecture of multiple disease epicenters (averaging 8.45±2.97 per patient) significantly explained individual gray matter atrophy patterns (44±16% variance) in depression, with shared epicenters (hippocampus, thalamus, medial frontal gyrus) showing higher participation coefficients and revealing two subgroups differing in age of onset.
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: Key findings are clearly summarized in the Abstract and Results sections.
Supporting Text: the structural connectome architecture of the identified disease epicenters significantly explained 44% (±16%) variance of gray matter atrophy... patients demonstrated tremendous interindividual variations... several disease epicenters with higher participation coefficient... including the hippocampus, thalamus, and medial frontal gyrus were significantly shared... the association between connectome and gray matter atrophy uncovered two distinct subgroups with different ages of onset.
Location: Abstract, Results section
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed:
Answer: The structural multi-epicenter model significantly outperformed other models (structural single-epicenter: R²=0.12±0.07; structural multi-epicenter: R²=0.44±0.16; functional single-epicenter: R²=0.22±0.03; functional multi-epicenter: R²=0.09±0.05; all paired t-test p<0.001). Patients averaged 8.45±2.97 disease epicenters with substantial interindividual variation in number and distribution. Significantly shared epicenters (permutation p<0.05 Bonferroni-corrected) included thalamus, hippocampus, striatum, medial frontal gyrus, and inferior frontal gyrus. These shared epicenters showed significantly higher participation coefficient than randomly selected regions (permutation p<0.001), but no significant difference in degree. Disease exposure (connectivity-weighted epicenter atrophy) significantly correlated with regional atrophy (mean Pearson R=0.50±0.12, all p<0.05 FDR-corrected). Spatial disease exposure showed no significant correlation, ruling out spatial proximity effects. K-means clustering identified two optimal subgroups (N=43 and N=62) with significant difference in age of onset (t=2.48, FDR-corrected p=0.044, Cohen's d=0.49). Replication dataset reproduced main findings, though age-of-onset difference was marginally significant (uncorrected p=0.081) due to limited young-onset cases (N=31 with onset ≤18 years).
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: Detailed results with statistical values are comprehensively reported throughout the Results section and Figure captions.
Supporting Text: The performance (the explained variance, R², mean±S.D.) of these four models was as follow: structural single-epicenter model (0.12±0.07), structural multi-epicenter model (0.44±0.16), functional single-epicenter model (0.22±0.03) and functional multi-epicenter model (0.09±0.05)... patients with depression had 8.45 (±2.97) disease epicenters... thalamus, hippocampus, striatum, medial frontal gyrus and inferior frontal gyrus (permutation testing p<0.05, Bonferroni corrected)... significantly higher PC than other brain regions (permutation testing p<0.001)... the regional disease exposure significantly correlated with gray matter atrophy pattern (Pearson's correlation R, 0.50±0.12, all p values <0.05, FDR corrected)... patients with depression were optimally clustered into two subgroups... significant differences in terms of age of onset (two sample t=2.48, FDR corrected p=0.044, cohen'd=0.49)
Location: Results section, lines 182-254; Figure 2, Figure 3, Figure 4 captions
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Answer: Study innovatively applies individualized normative modeling with GPR to derive per-region Z-scores, then uses backward stepwise regression to identify patient-specific multi-epicenter models explaining atrophy via structural covariance. Disease exposure metric quantifies connectivity-weighted vulnerability. Spatial disease exposure control (using Euclidean distance instead of connectivity) rules out trivial spatial proximity effects. Degree correlation with atrophy ruled out hub-driven confounding. Repeated k-means clustering on connectivity-atrophy correlation profiles reveals data-driven subgroups. Replication in independent medicated cohort strengthens findings despite medication and age distribution differences.

caa10_key_limitations.answer:
Answer: Limited clinical data prevented deeper investigation of how connectome-atrophy associations relate to clinical manifestations. Only patients without comorbid mental disorders were recruited, limiting generalizability to more heterogeneous clinical populations. In the replication dataset, all patients were medicated at scan time and detailed medication information was not recorded, precluding analysis of medication effects on findings.
Confidence Rating: High
Negative Answer Category: Not Negative
Reason: Limitations are explicitly described in the Discussion section.
Supporting Text: Our study has several limitations. First, we failed to record enough clinical data to deeply investigated whether and how the association between normal connectome architecture and gray matter atrophy underlay the clinical manifestation in depression. Second, only patients without other mental disorders comorbidities were recruited in this study. Future studies could recruit more heterogeneous samples to investigate the effect of comorbidity on these results. Third, in the replication dataset, all patients were taking medicine at the scan and we failed to record detailed information on medicine. Even our results suggested that findings derived from never-treated first-episode patients could be validated in patients who had taken antidepressants, we could not deeply investigate whether and how antidepressants affected these results.
Location: Discussion section, lines 265-267

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: The study uses the 246-region Brainnetome Atlas, with 4 regions excluded for low SNR (SNR<100), yielding 242 regions for final analyses. Both datasets acquired on 3T GE Discovery MR750 scanners with detailed acquisition parameters provided. Discovery dataset: TR/TE=8164/3.18ms for T1, voxel=1×1×1mm³; TR/TE=2000/40ms for fMRI. Replication dataset: TR/TE=5.92/1.956ms for T1, voxel=1×1×1mm³; TR/TE=2000/30ms for fMRI. Abstract mentions '297 patients' but Table 1 and Methods consistently report 105+106=211 patients total; the discrepancy is not explained. Discovery cohort consists of never-treated first-episode patients (mean age ~20 years), while replication cohort is medicated with older age distribution (mean ~33 years). Illness duration: Discovery mean 17.22 (SD 18.80) months; Replication mean 54.28 (SD 66.61) months. HAMD scores: Discovery mean 22.26 (SD 6.19); Replication mean 27.60 (SD 7.87). Age of onset: Discovery mean 16.81 (SD 4.40) years; Replication mean 28.70 (SD 11.55) years. Supplementary Tables S1-S3 provide detailed lists of disease epicenters for overall sample and subgroups 1 and 2. The paper emphasizes individual-level heterogeneity in epicenter number and distribution while identifying shared epicenters across patients. Ethical approval obtained from institutional committees of both sites. Sensitivity analyses found no significant correlation between model performance (R²) or disease exposure-atrophy association and IQR or education level.
